name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: MCP Server Maven Plugin is a Java 17 Apache Maven plugin for running a Machai Model Context Protocol server as part of a Maven build. It provides two aggregator goals for Maven reactors: stateless starts org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStatelessMcpServer and streamable starts org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStreamableMcpServer. Each goal applies configured parameter values as JVM system properties when the property is not already set, loads the Machai PropertiesConfigurator from mcp.config, uses the current Maven project name and version to create the server, sets the Maven base directory as the project directory, registers tools from the configuration, sets the required mcp.port, and starts the HTTP endpoint. This makes configured MCP tools available to MCP-compatible HTTP clients without a separate launcher, supporting local development, demonstrations, repeatable integration tests, and build-driven AI automation. Because both goals are aggregators, a multi-module reactor starts one server for the build instead of one server per module. Configuration-loading and server-start failures are reported as Maven execution errors.

features.name: stateless
features.description: Aggregator Maven goal implemented by org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.HttpStatelessServerMojo. It loads the configured server settings, creates org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStatelessMcpServer with Maven project metadata, configures its project directory and HTTP port, registers configured tools, and starts the stateless transport.

examples.description: Invoke the installed plugin by fully qualified Maven coordinates. Provide an available port and a readable Machai MCP properties file, then connect an MCP HTTP client while the Maven process is running.

features.name: streamable
features.description: Aggregator Maven goal implemented by org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.HttpStreamableMcpServerMojo. It performs the shared parameter and configuration processing, creates org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStreamableMcpServer, configures the project directory and HTTP port, registers configured tools, and starts the streamable HTTP transport.

examples.description: Start a streamable MCP HTTP endpoint with a selected port and configuration file. Configure a compatible client to use the endpoint after Maven has started the server.

features.name: applyParameters
features.description: Applies each configured params map entry to java.lang.System properties only if that property is not already set. This preserves explicit process-level settings while allowing plugin configuration to supply server-related values.

examples.description: Add a params entry to plugin configuration. During either server goal, it becomes a JVM system property unless the Maven process was already started with a value for the same property.

customizations.name: mcp.port
customizations.description: Required Maven property that selects the HTTP listening port used by either transport.

examples.description: Choose an available port when starting the server.

customizations.name: mcp.config
customizations.description: Maven property for the readable configuration file passed to the Machai MCP server configurator. Supply a valid path because startup loads the file.

examples.description: Keep environment-specific Machai server and tool settings in a separate properties file and pass its location at invocation time.

customizations.name: params
customizations.description: Map of additional values applied as JVM system properties only when the corresponding property is absent.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run a stateless MCP server
steps: Add the plugin coordinates org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.0 to the build plugins section, or invoke the plugin directly with its fully qualified Maven coordinates.
Create a readable Machai MCP properties file containing the server and tool settings required by the intended workflow.
Run mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.0:stateless -Dmcp.port=8080 -Dmcp.config=C:/config/mcp.properties from the target project or reactor root.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the endpoint configured by the Machai server and use the registered tools while Maven remains running.

examples.title: Run streamable HTTP for a multi-module build
steps: Resolve the plugin version 1.4.0 through Maven Central or declare it in the consuming project build.
Prepare the external MCP properties file and reserve an HTTP port.
At the reactor root, run mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.0:streamable -Dmcp.port=8080 -Dmcp.config=C:/config/mcp.properties.
Use a streamable HTTP MCP client against the single server started for the aggregator build.
